lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is weather and seasons — the favourite topic of every English person.
[laugh] Is it true that you talk about the weather all the time?
Completely true. In Manchester it rains a lot, but usually it's just drizzle — light rain that never stops.
That sounds a bit sad.
You get used to it. Nobody uses an umbrella. We just put our hood up and walk through the puddles.
Here in Baku, the problem isn't the rain. It's the wind. Baku is called the city of winds.
I noticed! On my first day, the wind took my hat into the sea.
[laugh] That's the Khazri, our north wind. In summer we love a light breeze from the sea, but in winter the wind is freezing.
And the summer here is so hot. In July there was a heatwave — forty degrees!
And very humid near the sea. You feel wet just walking to the shop.
And then you were under the weather last week. Was it the air conditioning?
Yes! Hot outside, ice-cold inside. I caught a cold in the office.
My mum always says that. Air conditioning is the enemy.
What's your favourite season?
Autumn. Cool air, golden trees. Perfect for running.
You run every day, don't you?
Come rain or shine! I'm training for the half marathon. Yesterday I ran in the rain and came home completely wet.
Didn't you check the forecast?
I did. It said sunny. The forecast is the biggest liar in the world.
[laugh] Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what's the weather like where you live today — and what's your favourite season, and why?
Mine is autumn — with a good raincoat. See you next time!
Bye for now!
